title: Measure a pin's diameter with a hand-held digital caliper, then put the caliper back on its rest
instruction: Measure the standing aluminium pin's diameter with the digital caliper, held in one hand off the bench: both jaws just touching the pin, not squeezed, so the display shows its diameter. Then lay the caliper back on its rest and move both hands away.
context: Checking a part's size with a hand-held caliper is a routine step in machining, inspection and lab work. The caliper must be held square to the part, and the jaw closed gently until both jaws just touch: a tilted caliper or a heavy thumb on the slider gives a wrong reading.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Pin, loose, 46 g: an aluminium cylinder 23.40 mm across and 40 mm long, standing on end at (0.27, 0.00). Rest, fixed: a wooden block 40 x 100 x 30 mm, x 0.283 to 0.323, y 0.10 to 0.20. Digital caliper (0 to 100 mm), loose, 134 g in all, lying flat on the rest with its jaws pointing at the robots and its head overhanging the rest's left end: a stainless beam 16 mm wide and 3.5 mm thick along y (x 0.295 to 0.311, y 0.060 to 0.285), its underside on the rest, 30 mm above the table. Fixed jaw near the beam's left end: a stainless plate 45 x 8 x 3.5 mm reaching from the beam's front edge towards the robots (x 0.250 to 0.295), level with the beam, measuring face at y = 0.250 facing right; the beam goes on 35 mm past it (the head). Sliding jaw: the same plate, its face at y = 0.210 (jaws 40 mm apart at the start). Slider: a dark grey housing 38 x 77 mm and 9 mm tall on top of the beam (x 0.293 to 0.331, y 0.131 to 0.208 at the start), carrying a grey-green screen 20 x 50 mm with four dark 7-segment digits 14 mm tall, tops away from the robots, a decimal point after the second: the jaw gap in mm to 0.01 mm (tens blank under 10 mm), 40.00 at the start; a red ZERO and a black ON/OFF button (not used); and at its right end a black thumb rest 20 x 6 mm, 16 mm tall above the beam (its right face at y = 0.125 at the start). The slider moves along y with 0.6 N of friction, gap 0 to 99 mm; pushing the thumb rest left closes the jaws. For real trials the pin is a force-sensing pin of the same size and mass: a split aluminium sleeve, 23.40 mm across, around a 10 N miniature button load cell across its diameter (0.02 N resolution), its thin cable out of its top end to a logger; the scored force is its reading when the display is photographed. No other objects.
scoring: The measurement is taken while the caliper is held: at any moment when the caliper is held (a fingertip within 20 mm of its beam, and no part of it within 3 mm of the table or of the rest), the pin is between its jaws (the pin's axis upright within 30 degrees of the jaws' normal, crossing the jaws' mid-plane between the two measuring faces, at least 2 mm in from the jaw tips and at least 2 mm from either end of the pin), the caliper and the pin have moved under 1 mm (any point on them) over the last second, and both fingertips of the other hand are 80 mm or more from the caliper and the pin. The latest such moment counts. Its score: 0.1; 0.25 if the display reads within 1.00 mm of 23.40; 0.5 if within 0.20 mm, the pin's axis within 3 degrees of parallel to the jaw faces and the sliding jaw pressing on it with at most 2 N; 1.0 if within 0.05 mm, within 1 degree and at most 0.3 N. The score is 0 unless such a measurement was taken and, at the end of the trial, the caliper lies back on its rest (over the rest, its lowest point within 3 mm of the rest's top, flat within 5 degrees, clear of the table), all four fingertips of both hands are 80 mm or more from the caliper and the pin, and the caliper and the pin moved under 1 mm in the last second. The jaw force is the force squeezing the pin across its diameter, at rest: in simulation it is the reaction in the rigid sliding jaw's mounting, averaged over half a second; in a real trial it is read from the force-sensing pin (see setup) at the moment the display is photographed.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the pin on end at (0.27, 0.00); slide the jaws open until the display reads 40.00 and lay the caliper back on its rest.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. The caliper is a loose body with rigid jaws; its slider is a damped slide with 0.6 N of friction, and the display shows its position. The jaw force is read from the reaction where the sliding jaw is fixed to the slider, like a load cell there. Pad contacts on the beam use an 8 mm contact patch. The digits are larger than a real caliper's. The pin is an ideal cylinder.
